subproblem.title: Fubini exchange for a primitive composed with a measurable radius (common core of parent Steps 8 and 9)
subproblem.statement: Let (X, 𝒜) be a measurable space (formally a type X : Type, which covers both uses X = ℝ and X = ℝ^{n+ℓ}), ν an s-finite measure on X, S ∈ 𝒜, r: X → ℝ measurable, g: X → ℝ, F, F′: ℝ → ℝ and σ, ρ ∈ ℝ. Assume r(x) ∈ (σ, ρ] for every x ∈ S, g is ν-integrable on S, F′ is Lebesgue integrable on (σ, ρ], and F(t) = F(σ) + ∫_{(σ,t]} F′(τ)dτ for every t ∈ [σ, ρ]. Then (a) x ↦ g(x)(F(r(x)) − F(σ)) is ν-integrable on S; (b) t ↦ F′(t)·∫_{S ∩ {x : t < r(x)}} g dν is Lebesgue integrable on (σ, ρ]; and (c) ∫_{(σ,ρ]} F′(t)(∫_{S ∩ {x : t < r(x)}} g dν)dt = ∫_S g(x)(F(r(x)) − F(σ))dν(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (ν : Measure X) (S : Set X) (r g : X → ℝ) (F F' : ℝ → ℝ) (σ ρ : ℝ), SFinite ν → MeasurableSet S → Measurable r → (∀ x ∈ S, r x ∈ Ioc σ ρ) → IntegrableOn g S ν → IntegrableOn F' (Ioc σ ρ) → (∀ t ∈ Icc σ ρ, F t = F σ + ∫ τ in Ioc σ t, F' τ) → IntegrableOn (fun x ↦ g x * (F (r x) - F σ)) S ν ∧ IntegrableOn (fun t ↦ F' t * ∫ x in S ∩ {x | t < r x}, g x ∂ν) (Ioc σ ρ) ∧ ∫ t in Ioc σ ρ, F' t * ∫ x in S ∩ {x | t < r x}, g x ∂ν = ∫ x in S, g x * (F (r x) - F σ) ∂ν
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. Notation. λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ and λ_I := λ⌞(σ, ρ], a finite measure (λ((σ, ρ]) = max(ρ − σ, 0) < ∞); ν_S := ν⌞S, which is s-finite because ν is. For t ∈ ℝ put T_t := {x ∈ X : t < r(x)}, and put T := {(t, x) ∈ ℝ × X : t < r(x)}. All integrals are Bochner (Lebesgue) integrals of real-valued functions; Fubini's theorem is applied below only to an integrable function on the product.
2. Measurability. The maps (t, x) ↦ t and (t, x) ↦ r(x) are measurable on ℝ × X with the product σ-algebra, so T = {(t, x) : t < r(x)} is measurable. Likewise every T_t = r⁻¹((t, ∞)) is measurable in X, and every interval (−∞, u) is Borel in ℝ.
3. Product integrand. Let Ψ(t, x) := F′(t)g(x) and Φ := 1_T·Ψ, i.e. Φ(t, x) = F′(t)g(x) if t < r(x) and Φ(t, x) = 0 otherwise. Since F′ ∈ L¹(λ_I) and g ∈ L¹(ν_S), Ψ is λ_I ⊗ ν_S-integrable: it is a.e.-strongly measurable as the product of an a.e.-strongly measurable function of t and one of x, and by Tonelli's theorem (valid for s-finite factors) ∫∫|Ψ| d(λ_I ⊗ ν_S) = (∫_{(σ,ρ]}|F′|dλ)·(∫_S|g|dν) < ∞. Because T is measurable (step 2), Φ = 1_T·Ψ is also λ_I ⊗ ν_S-integrable.
4. Fubini. Both factors λ_I and ν_S are s-finite and Φ ∈ L¹(λ_I ⊗ ν_S), so Fubini's theorem, which holds for s-finite (not only σ-finite) factors, gives: (i) x ↦ ∫Φ(t, x)dλ_I(t) is ν_S-integrable; (ii) t ↦ ∫Φ(t, x)dν_S(x) is λ_I-integrable; (iii) ∫(∫Φ(t, x)dν_S(x))dλ_I(t) = ∫(∫Φ(t, x)dλ_I(t))dν_S(x).
5. Sections at fixed t. For all t ∈ ℝ and x ∈ X, Φ(t, x) = F′(t)·(1_{T_t}g)(x). Pulling out the constant F′(t) and using that T_t is measurable (step 2), ∫Φ(t, x)dν_S(x) = F′(t)∫_S 1_{T_t}g dν = F′(t)∫_{S∩T_t} g dν for every t ∈ ℝ.
6. Sections at fixed x ∈ S. For x ∈ S and t ∈ ℝ, Φ(t, x) = g(x)·(1_{(−∞, r(x))}F′)(t). Hence ∫Φ(t, x)dλ_I(t) = g(x)∫_{(σ,ρ]∩(−∞,r(x))} F′dλ. Because r(x) ∈ (σ, ρ] we have (σ, ρ] ∩ (−∞, r(x)) = (σ, r(x)) (if σ < t < r(x) then t < ρ). The sets (σ, r(x)) and (σ, r(x)] differ by the λ-null set {r(x)}, so ∫_{(σ,r(x))}F′ = ∫_{(σ,r(x)]}F′, and the hypothesis on F at the point t = r(x) ∈ (σ, ρ] ⊆ [σ, ρ] gives ∫_{(σ,r(x)]}F′ = F(r(x)) − F(σ). Therefore ∫Φ(t, x)dλ_I(t) = g(x)(F(r(x)) − F(σ)) for every x ∈ S.
7. Conclusion (a). By step 6 the ν_S-integrable function of step 4(i) coincides with x ↦ g(x)(F(r(x)) − F(σ)) at every point of S. Since S is measurable, ν_S-almost every point lies in S, so the two functions are ν_S-a.e. equal; hence x ↦ g(x)(F(r(x)) − F(σ)) is ν-integrable on S.
8. Conclusion (b). By step 5 the λ_I-integrable function of step 4(ii) equals t ↦ F′(t)∫_{S∩T_t} g dν at every t ∈ ℝ, so the latter is Lebesgue integrable on (σ, ρ].
9. Conclusion (c). ∫_{(σ,ρ]}F′(t)(∫_{S∩T_t} g dν)dt = ∫(∫Φ(t, x)dν_S(x))dλ_I(t) by step 5, = ∫(∫Φ(t, x)dλ_I(t))dν_S(x) by step 4(iii), = ∫_S g(x)(F(r(x)) − F(σ))dν(x) by step 6, because the two integrands agree at every point of the measurable set S. ∎
proof_key_steps: T := {(t, x) : t < r(x)} is product-measurable and Φ(t, x) := 1_T(t, x)F′(t)g(x) is integrable for λ⌞(σ,ρ] ⊗ ν⌞S, being the restriction to T of the integrable product F′(t)g(x)
Fubini: both partial integrals of Φ are integrable and the two iterated integrals agree
t-section: ∫Φ(t, ·)dν⌞S = F′(t)∫_{S∩{t<r}} g dν for every t
x-section for x ∈ S: (σ, ρ] ∩ (−∞, r(x)) = (σ, r(x)); drop the null endpoint r(x) and use F(r(x)) = F(σ) + ∫_{(σ,r(x)]}F′ to get g(x)(F(r(x)) − F(σ))
Transfer the integrability statements and the identity through the two section formulas (a.e. on ν⌞S, pointwise in t)

subproblem.title: Fubini on the annulus: ∫_{(σ,ρ]} F′(t)(∫_{B_ρ∖B_t} w dμ)dt = ∫_A w(F(|x−ξ|) − F(σ))dμ (parent Step 8)
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Borel σ-algebra, Euclidean norm) that is finite on compact sets, ξ ∈ E, w: E → ℝ, F, F′: ℝ → ℝ and σ, ρ ∈ ℝ. Write B_t := {x ∈ E : |x − ξ| ≤ t} for the closed ball and A := B_ρ∖B_σ. Assume w is μ-integrable on A, F′ is Lebesgue integrable on (σ, ρ], and F(t) = F(σ) + ∫_{(σ,t]} F′(τ)dτ for every t ∈ [σ, ρ]. Then (a) x ↦ w(x)(F(|x − ξ|) − F(σ)) is μ-integrable on A; (b) t ↦ F′(t)·∫_{B_ρ∖B_t} w dμ is Lebesgue integrable on (σ, ρ]; and (c) ∫_{(σ,ρ]} F′(t)(∫_{B_ρ∖B_t} w dμ)dt = ∫_A w(x)(F(|x − ξ|) − F(σ))dμ(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (ξ : Ambient n ℓ) (w : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (F F' : ℝ → ℝ) (σ ρ : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → IntegrableOn w (closedBall ξ ρ \ closedBall ξ σ) μ → IntegrableOn F' (Ioc σ ρ) → (∀ t ∈ Icc σ ρ, F t = F σ + ∫ τ in Ioc σ t, F' τ) → IntegrableOn (fun x ↦ w x * (F ‖x - ξ‖ - F σ)) (closedBall ξ ρ \ closedBall ξ σ) μ ∧ IntegrableOn (fun t ↦ F' t * ∫ x in closedBall ξ ρ \ closedBall ξ t, w x ∂μ) (Ioc σ ρ) ∧ ∫ t in Ioc σ ρ, F' t * ∫ x in closedBall ξ ρ \ closedBall ξ t, w x ∂μ = ∫ x in closedBall ξ ρ \ closedBall ξ σ, w x * (F ‖x - ξ‖ - F σ) ∂μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. μ is s-finite. E is σ-compact: E = ⋃_{k∈ℕ} B_k, and each closed ball B_k is compact (Heine–Borel). As μ is finite on compact sets, μ(B_k) < ∞ for all k, so μ is σ-finite and in particular s-finite.
2. Measurability. A = B_ρ∖B_σ is Borel (a difference of two closed sets), and r(x) := |x − ξ| is continuous, hence Borel measurable.
3. Range of r on A. If x ∈ A then x ∈ B_ρ gives r(x) ≤ ρ and x ∉ B_σ gives r(x) > σ; so r(x) ∈ (σ, ρ] for every x ∈ A.
4. Apply the sibling lemma primitive_fubini (mcm_primitive_radial_fubini) with X := E, ν := μ, S := A, r := |· − ξ|, g := w and the given F, F′, σ, ρ: its hypotheses are steps 1–3 together with the assumed integrability of w on A, of F′ on (σ, ρ], and the representation of F. It yields (a) verbatim, and also (b′) t ↦ F′(t)∫_{A∩{x : t<r(x)}} w dμ is Lebesgue integrable on (σ, ρ], and (c′) ∫_{(σ,ρ]}F′(t)(∫_{A∩{x : t<r(x)}} w dμ)dt = ∫_A w(x)(F(|x − ξ|) − F(σ))dμ(x).
5. Set identity. For every t ∈ (σ, ρ], A ∩ {x : t < r(x)} = B_ρ∖B_t. Indeed, if x ∈ A and t < r(x), then x ∈ B_ρ and x ∉ B_t. Conversely, if x ∈ B_ρ and x ∉ B_t, then r(x) > t > σ, so x ∉ B_σ; thus x ∈ A and t < r(x).
6. Conclusion. By step 5, for every t ∈ (σ, ρ] we have F′(t)∫_{A∩{t<r}} w dμ = F′(t)∫_{B_ρ∖B_t} w dμ. Two functions that agree at every point of the measurable set (σ, ρ] are simultaneously integrable on (σ, ρ] and have the same integral over it. Hence (b′) gives (b) and (c′) gives (c). ∎
proof_key_steps: μ finite on compacts and E = ⋃_k B_k with B_k compact ⇒ μ σ-finite, hence s-finite
A is Borel, r = |· − ξ| is continuous, and r(A) ⊆ (σ, ρ]
Apply primitive_fubini with (X, ν, S, r, g) = (E, μ, A, |· − ξ|, w)
For σ < t ≤ ρ: A ∩ {x : t < |x − ξ|} = B_ρ∖B_t
Replace the t-integrand on (σ, ρ] to obtain (b) and (c)

subproblem.title: Fubini on the triangle: ∫_{(σ,ρ]} F′(t)(∫_{(t,ρ]} e)dt = ∫_{(σ,ρ]} e(F − F(σ)) (parent Step 9)
subproblem.statement: Let e, F, F′: ℝ → ℝ and σ, ρ ∈ ℝ. Assume e and F′ are Lebesgue integrable on (σ, ρ] and F(t) = F(σ) + ∫_{(σ,t]} F′(τ)dτ for every t ∈ [σ, ρ]. Then (a) s ↦ e(s)(F(s) − F(σ)) is Lebesgue integrable on (σ, ρ]; (b) t ↦ F′(t)·∫_{(t,ρ]} e(τ)dτ is Lebesgue integrable on (σ, ρ]; and (c) ∫_{(σ,ρ]} F′(t)(∫_{(t,ρ]} e(τ)dτ)dt = ∫_{(σ,ρ]} e(s)(F(s) − F(σ))ds.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (e F F' : ℝ → ℝ) (σ ρ : ℝ), IntegrableOn e (Ioc σ ρ) → IntegrableOn F' (Ioc σ ρ) → (∀ t ∈ Icc σ ρ, F t = F σ + ∫ τ in Ioc σ t, F' τ) → IntegrableOn (fun s ↦ e s * (F s - F σ)) (Ioc σ ρ) ∧ IntegrableOn (fun t ↦ F' t * ∫ τ in Ioc t ρ, e τ) (Ioc σ ρ) ∧ ∫ t in Ioc σ ρ, F' t * ∫ τ in Ioc t ρ, e τ = ∫ s in Ioc σ ρ, e s * (F s - F σ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. Hypotheses of the abstract lemma. Lebesgue measure λ on ℝ is σ-finite, hence s-finite; S := (σ, ρ] is Borel; r := id_ℝ is measurable; and r(s) = s ∈ (σ, ρ] for every s ∈ S.
2. Apply the sibling lemma primitive_fubini (mcm_primitive_radial_fubini) with X := ℝ, ν := λ, S := (σ, ρ], r := id, g := e and the given F, F′, σ, ρ (e is integrable on S = (σ, ρ] by assumption). It yields (a) verbatim, and also (b′) t ↦ F′(t)∫_{(σ,ρ]∩{s : t<s}} e(s)ds is Lebesgue integrable on (σ, ρ], and (c′) ∫_{(σ,ρ]}F′(t)(∫_{(σ,ρ]∩{s : t<s}} e(s)ds)dt = ∫_{(σ,ρ]} e(s)(F(s) − F(σ))ds.
3. Set identity. For every t ∈ (σ, ρ], (σ, ρ] ∩ {s : t < s} = (t, ρ]: if σ < s ≤ ρ and t < s then s ∈ (t, ρ]; conversely, if t < s ≤ ρ then s > t > σ, so s ∈ (σ, ρ] and t < s.
4. Conclusion. By step 3 the t-integrands of (b′), (c′) coincide with t ↦ F′(t)∫_{(t,ρ]} e at every point of the measurable set (σ, ρ]; functions agreeing on (σ, ρ] are simultaneously integrable there and have the same integral over it. Hence (b′) gives (b) and (c′) gives (c). ∎
proof_key_steps: Lebesgue measure is s-finite, S = (σ, ρ] is Borel, r = id is measurable and maps S into (σ, ρ]
Apply primitive_fubini with (X, ν, S, r, g) = (ℝ, λ, (σ, ρ], id, e)
For σ < t ≤ ρ: (σ, ρ] ∩ {s : t < s} = (t, ρ]
Replace the t-integrand on (σ, ρ] to obtain (b) and (c)
